preregistration: this file, committed before any generation (record-first). Source: one21labs/one21tools#328, re-measure section. Owner answers 25-Oct-2026, in-session: revision 2 'Approve as written'; domain read 'Me (owner)'.
hypothesis: Neutral (ADR 0059): appending the control-narratives revision 2 body to the system prompt may raise, lower, or leave unchanged the graded fraction of expectations met, versus the same model with no skill, on Claude Opus 5.5 and on Claude Sonnet 5.5. A null, a harmful result, or a model-dependent result are equally valid recorded outcomes.

arms.without: claude -p --model <M> --effort medium, isolation flags (--tools "", --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config, shared deny list), empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, cwd outside the checkout; hermetic_driver.NEUTRAL_FRAME + task text on stdin; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=32000
arms.with: without + --append-system-prompt = treatments/control-narratives.txt (revision 2 SKILL.md body at source_sha, frontmatter stripped)

auth: The empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR used by every generation cell and by the Opus judge holds no credentials, so each call authenticates from CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, which hermetic_driver.build_env passes through (hermetic_driver.KEEP). `claude auth status` reports any non-empty token as signed in, so check_auth tests the token with one call to a model that does not exist: the API answers 401 to a bad token and 404 to a good one, at $0 either way (measured 26-Oct-2026, CLI 2.1.310). The owner creates the token with `claude setup-token` and exports it before the prescreen.
effort: medium for both models, as 2026-10-12, so the model is the only thing that varies across the model factor.
harness: one21labs/skill-measure, loaded from $SKILL_MEASURE_ROOT (benchmarks/README.md). The commit used (benchmarks/README.md:23) is captured by prep.py as harness_sha in treatments/costs.json at freeze (first freeze only). Every prescreen, pilot, grid and grading run uses that commit, which must be clean (no -dirty suffix) and reachable on skill-measure's origin; a run at any other commit is a deviation the README records with its SHA.

evals.authoring: 9 tasks by a separate agent forbidden to read any repository file, given only the skill's one-line description; held out from revision 2, which was written from #328 before the tasks existed. Every task carries the expectation in evals.universal_expectation, appended verbatim (#328, reworded by the 2026-10-26 amendment).
evals.domain_read: Before the prescreen, the owner strikes every expectation that rewards what the receiving engineer would reject, above all an invented setpoint or trip value (skill-measure pre-registration.md, 'Audit the expectations against the reader'). Struck expectations are recorded in strikes.json and removed from the frozen battery; nothing else is edited. Order: the authored battery is committed to skills/control-narratives/evals/evals.json, the strikes are removed from that file in a later commit, and only then does prep.py freeze it (prep.py refuses to re-freeze a changed battery).
evals.provenance_0101: ADR 0101 decision 1 splits the delta by eval provenance. Every eval here is blind-authored, so the split has one stratum (blind, all evals) and each per-model delta is reported under that label. One expectation per eval is not blind: the universal expectation was authored with the skill in view (#328 wrote it beside revision 2). The per-eval split cannot separate it. invented.py, the secondary metric, counts the same failure by script, which ADR 0101 holds immune to coupling. overlap.json: overlap.py reports n-gram containment of the expectations in the frozen treatment minus the mean over the repo's other skills, separately for the blind expectations and the universal one (a floor, #317).
evals.universal_expectation: States no number the task did not give.

prescreen.rule: 1 bare rep per eval per model, graded BEFORE any with-arm cell. Bare fraction-met >= 0.85 = saturated -> dropped for that model only. 0.0 floors flagged, kept. Prescreen cells are never reused in the grid.
prescreen.g_floor: a model with fewer than 8 surviving evals still runs, labelled DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY (ADR 0095 decision 4)

pilot.rule: 2 with-arm cells per model on the first eval; per-cell estimate and prior spend derived by grid.py prior_costs (cost.estimate_scope); grid refused if projected > remaining ceiling (ADR 0073)

grid: surviving evals x {with, without} x {opus, sonnet} x 2 reps; at most 9 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 72 cells. A reply cut off at the output cap is scored failed on every expectation with no judge call (owner, 26-Oct-2026: a truncated narrative is unusable to the receiving engineer), is never regenerated, and the per-arm cap-hit count is reported beside the verdict.
judging: Primary: one cross-family judge, whichever is available; grok is one option among several (owner, 26-Oct-2026). It is resolved by `probe_sandbox.py --judges auto` before the prescreen: skill-measure's auto order takes the first backend that answers a probe, $SKILL_BENCH_JUDGE_CMD + $SKILL_BENCH_JUDGE_MODEL first (a ChatGPT CLI or a local model), then grok, then copilot. The resolved backend is recorded in graded/sandbox-probe.jsonl and named explicitly to grade.py for every grading pass, so the judge is fixed before any data. Its verdict is what can promote (ADR 0093); every grok or copilot grade is read back for the answering model's family and a same-family or unplaceable answer is an error row (copilot's auto can route to Claude); a command judge cannot report who answered, so it is placed once, from the model $SKILL_BENCH_JUDGE_MODEL declares. A local model must be placeable by skill-measure's family table (open-weight families need the harness commit that adds them). Secondary: Claude Opus 5.5 isolated identically, FRAME-UNCHECKED. If no cross-family backend answers, the Opus result is reported unpromoted and the README says so (it still counts for the decision rule). Prescreen selection uses the Opus judge (selection only, no verdict). Before any grade, probe_sandbox.py runs a planted-file probe through each judge's grade() path on the installed CLI; rows go to graded/sandbox-probe.jsonl, and a LEAK halts grading until the sandbox is fixed (a deny flag is not evidence on its own, #331).
metrics: per model: eval-clustered mean of (with - without) fraction-met, mean over reps within eval; benchstats.keep_verdict (KEEP iff 95% t-interval lower bound > 0, HARMFUL iff upper < 0, else INCONCLUSIVE; practical bar 0). Primary: the 2 per-model verdicts under the primary judge. Secondary, descriptive: the per-cell count of numbers absent from the task (the invented-value failure #328 names), per arm. Secondary, descriptive: per-arm consistency (mean within-eval rep SD and mean worst-rep score; skill-measure pre-registration.md, 'Variance is a primary metric'). Secondary, descriptive: citation accuracy. invented.py lists, per cell, the standards it cites that neither its task nor the treatment gave. Each distinct designation is checked once against the standards body's own catalog (exists; edition; scope supports what it is cited for) by a web-research pass with an adversarial re-check, recorded in graded/citation-check.json; the owner confirms that table. Reported per arm: cells citing at least one standard that does not exist or does not cover what it is cited for. The treatment's own citations were checked the same way before freeze (PR #337).
multiplicity: 2 primary intervals at 95% each, no correction.
power: Practical bar 0 (metrics). The scenario count is fixed by the battery (G <= 9), not sized from a prior. At 80% power (skill-measure benchstats.clusters_for), G=9 reliably calls a true delta of 0.26 at the house spread 0.24 (pre-registration.md sizing table), and G=8 calls 0.28. From #328's 18-Oct intervals via benchstats.sd_between (sd: Sonnet 0.19 at G=9, Opus 0.09 at G=6; other tasks and other text, so a floor, not a plan), G=9 calls 0.21 on Sonnet and 0.10 on Opus. A smaller true effect has under 80% power and can return INCONCLUSIVE. A CI half-width is the 50%-power point, not a detectable effect.
comparison_to_2026-10-18: The 18-Oct live-text measurement's tasks and cells were lost with their branch (#328). Its numbers are context only; no delta is computed across the two instruments.

cost.estimate_basis: 2026-10-12 per-cell means: generation opus $0.063, sonnet $0.024; Opus judge $0.040 per cell. 94 generation cells plus up to 2 judges: about $10-20. #328's estimate was about $30.
cost.estimate_scope: grid.py prior_costs derives the per-cell estimate (generation mean of the prescreen and pilot cells, plus the Opus judge's measured cost per call) and the spend before the grid (those cells plus every judge pass on them); nothing is hand-filled. grid.py's backstop counts generation spend only; judge spend is recorded by grade.py and counts answered calls only (a judge call that times out records $0; a cross-family CLI reports no cost).

grid.py: the harness loads from $SKILL_MEASURE_ROOT (was SKILL_MEASURE_LIB). Each call is charged its measured cost plus any retried attempt, or an estimate when a failed call reports none (cost_gate.DEFAULT_FAILED_CALL_CHARGE_USD, $0.15, in the prescreen and pilot; the per-cell estimate in the grid). An overwritten ERROR cell's prior attempts are kept (prior_attempts_usd). Before each launch, recorded spend plus in-flight reservations plus the call's estimate must fit the cap (cost_gate.admit).

decision_rule: Owner, 26-Oct-2026, before generation. KEEP on a model: revision 2 stays. INCONCLUSIVE: revision 2 stays ('Inconclusive keeps it'). The Opus judge's verdict counts when no cross-family judge answers, labelled unpromoted ('Yes, Opus counts'). A HARMFUL verdict on any model (owner correction, 26-Oct-2026: 'find out why and correct it so that it is at least neutral or helpful'): the judge's per-expectation reasons for the harmed model's with-arm cells are read to find the mechanism, the README records it, and a revision 3 targets it. Revision 3 is measured as a NEW pre-registered dated dir on a NEW blind battery (a revision written from this battery's reasons would be scored on its own training tasks), on both models, and is accepted only when no model is HARMFUL. Until then this PR does not merge (owner choice b), and the PR records the mechanism and the follow-up dir.
